source.reported_origin: Profiling showed that attention-only HMA models exposed multiple CPU tensors even when their per-group views shared one allocation. The PR reported 12 tensors and about 144.37 ms CPU-hit latency for gpt-oss versus one tensor and about 124.95 ms with packed HMA; Gemma used four versus one tensor with nearly flat latency. The implementation was intentionally opt-in and retained the existing DeepSeek V4 packed path.

behaviors: the opt-in environment setting parses predictably and defaults off
default multi-group, single-group, and existing DeepSeek V4 layouts retain their behavior
enabled multi-group HMA layouts share one backing allocation across equal and varied page sizes
per-view offsets and block strides partition each row without cross-view or cross-block corruption
usable block capacity remains unchanged by packing and all layers remain represented exactly once
Simple CPU offload counts packed storage once and preserves offset and stride metadata
partially strided invalid layouts are rejected
connector registration exposes one canonical packed tensor and one full-row reference per group
verifier_contract.collection_integrity: JUnit must contain at least 22 passing, unique, non-skipped cases including varied page sizes, CPU capacity, canonical connector registration, and invalid partial-stride handling.

real_lifecycle_boundary.kind: real KV layout planning through torch shared-storage views, connector canonical registration, Simple CPU mirror derivation, and selected block row round-trip
real_lifecycle_boundary.entrypoint: get_kv_cache_config_from_groups -> torch.as_strided views -> OffloadingConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches -> CanonicalKVCaches -> SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler._derive_cpu_config -> CPU row copy and restore
real_lifecycle_boundary.limitation: The environment is CPU-only, so the verifier executes the complete layout, registration, addressing, capacity, and byte round-trip contract but does not launch CUDA/XPU DMA handlers.
